# Deal Screening

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. Screening is a first filter, not a diligence opinion: a deal that passes can still lose money, there is a real risk of loss in any private equity transaction, and no score here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the deal screening skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it when a teaser arrives, inbound or proactively sourced, in a sponsored auction or a proprietary process, and you need a rapid, defensible recommendation in one sitting. The method ingests the teaser or CIM executive summary (sector, revenue and EBITDA, growth, business model, process type and timeline, ownership and stated reason for sale) and flags hard stops at once: regulated industry or geography outside the fund mandate, size outside the target cheque range, obvious ESG exclusions. It then tests thesis fit on sector, stage and scale, and return profile (at a sector-normal entry multiple, can a five-year hold deliver the fund target on conservative assumptions). Market sizing runs a top-down and bottom-up cross-check and flags the sizing as a risk when the two are more than three times apart, business quality is scored green, amber or red with one line of evidence each (revenue quality, customer concentration, gross margin, management, moat, organic growth stripped of M&A, working capital), and a preliminary financial pass computes LTM EBITDA and margin, growth...
